A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EgoExo-Con and View-GRPO. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and can be matched across renumbering. Revised benchmark counts and settings require caution when interpreting performance differences.

before.justification: v1 reports original model and human evaluations, supervised fine-tuning and View-GRPO experiments, judge comparisons, and appendix analyses of encoder training and dataset subsets.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds reward ablations, another backbone, external benchmark evaluations, reasoning-length experiments and token-entropy analyses.

M1.justification: In v1, the reasoning reward measures similarity to reference reasoning using an LLM judge. v2 Section 5.2 adds explicit coupling between generated reasoning from paired viewpoints: spaCy extracts action and object sets, whose Jaccard overlaps form a structural reward. This is combined with reference similarity using lambda, changing the training objective.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates temporal verification and grounding on EgoExo-Con. v2 additionally evaluates general video question answering on Video-MME and grounding with diverse query formulations on TVGBench (Table 5). The three source datasets underlying EgoExo-Con remain CharadesEgo, EgoExo-4D and LEMMA.

E2.justification: InternVL3.5-8B, previously only cited, becomes an evaluated baseline against its View-GRPO adaptation in v2 Table 3. The existing benchmark comparators and Qwen SFT/GRPO comparisons remain. The external evaluations use already represented methods: TimeChat, TimeSuite and Qwen2.5-VL.

E3.justification: Reported benchmark accounting changes from 491 video pairs and 3,178 queries to 1,148 videos and 2,269 queries; the PDFs do not explain whether this reflects data revision or corrected accounting. Appendix B.3 changes the stated maximum pixel budget from 14 x 16 x 16 to 2.8 million. v2 also adds 2,000-step reasoning-length experiments and external evaluation protocols, and corrects the grounding-consistency inequality from IoU < 0.5 to IoU >= 0.5. These reported revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds a reward-component ablation distinguishing semantic-only from semantic-plus-structural rewards (Table 4), tests reasoning lengths and optimization stability (Appendix C.3), and extends the existing qualitative example with baseline responses and token-entropy comparisons (Section 5.5). The judge-size, encoder-freezing and subset analyses from v1 remain.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 8 introduces token-level predictive entropy for baseline, View-GRPO and reference reasoning, adding predictive-uncertainty reporting to the qualitative example. Neither version reports benchmark confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run/seed counts; the new entropy plots do not establish uncertainty in aggregate performance estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds InternVL3.5, external-benchmark, reward-ablation and reasoning-length results. Its full Qwen 7B method reports V-ExoEgo/G-ExoEgo of 45.1/18.7, versus 44.7/18.3 in v1; the latter values are retained as the semantic-only ablation in v2 Table 4. Table 5 newly reports Video-MME scores of 69.7 for View-GRPO versus 61.1 for Qwen2.5-VL. Tables 1–2 and the original appendix tables retain their numbers. Method and reported setting changes prevent treating revised headline scores as controlled, same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds mathematical definitions for counterpart-view reasoning, the action/object structural reward and its weighted combination with semantic similarity (Equations 5–7). The GRPO background and format/accuracy reward mathematics remain substantively unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central benchmark contribution, findings about cross-view inconsistency and inadequacy of naive multi-view fine-tuning remain. v2's introduction additionally claims generalization to other video-understanding benchmarks, extending the claimed applicability beyond the evidence presented in v1.

C2.justification: v2 extends the existing LLM-judge caveat with specific explanations involving insufficient short reasoning, hallucination or over-exploration in long reasoning, and rewards favoring verbosity over correctness (Appendix C.3). Appendix D adds discussion of synchronized-data costs and limitations of processing views independently. Sections 5.4–5.5 also interpret transfer results and entropy patterns as evidence of stronger temporal reasoning.

D1.justification: v2 specifies spaCy extraction, lambda = 0.7, frozen visual encoders and the selected 256-token reasoning length, while revising the pixel-budget statement and removing v1's model-specific training-time estimates. Resources are described as available rather than forthcoming. Appendix F clarifies that released video-related material consists of annotations and metadata, and identifies compensated in-lab annotators. External availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds comparison with EgoExo-Learn and cites Dou et al. on deriving egocentric-style data from exocentric videos. It sharpens positioning against EgoExoBench by additionally emphasizing the absence of a concrete improvement method there. The broader related-work organization and research positioning remain similar.

P1.justification: Most existing sections and much of their wording are retained. v2 makes localized rewrites, updates author affiliations and citation style, adds a qualitative-analysis subsection, and inserts Discussion and Ethics review appendices. Existing visualization material is renumbered and moved without a wholesale narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: v2 substantially changes typography, headers, text-block dimensions and figure placement. It adds an evaluation-setup diagram, redraws dataset statistics and the method diagram, expands the qualitative figure with baseline and entropy panels, adds reasoning-length plots and two tables, and extends Table 3. Several appendix figures and tables are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: The reward ablation, external-benchmark tests and reasoning-length analysis provide useful validation and concrete failure analysis absent in v1. Correcting the consistency inequality also improves clarity. These benefits are moderated by unexplained benchmark-count and pixel-budget revisions alongside unchanged comparison tables, which limit reproducibility and direct interpretation of version-to-version performance differences.
